a_single_cell_vs_pooled.answer: only the pooled 3-run n=144 is an admissible p95 reading: a 47/48-turn cell has n*(1-q)=2.4 < 3 and the estimator refuses it by name, so no single cell in the grid can carry the H1 comparison. The separation the prior card measured at n=48 survives as a diagnostic (100.0%% of paired resamples, floor ignored) but is not publishable; at n=144 the pair separates in 100.0%% of paired resamples. Pooling buys admissibility, not separation.

c_effective_n.answer: turn-n lag-1 is 0.3921 pooled (Fisher-z, 13 sets) and 0.4598 median; on the H1 pair it is 0.6423 (pointer-stable) and 0.1071 (transcript-grow). n_eff(144) = 62.89 under the pooled r (clears 60 by 2.9, 4.8%), 53.29 under the median r (does not), and 31.36 under pointer-stable's own r (does not, half the floor). The floor has to be met by the arm whose interval must be the tight one, so the answer is NO: 144 raw turns are worth 31.36 effective timings on the C arm.

grid_under_test.note: the prior card's 'pooled 3-rep 144' IS the launch grid's pair n; it is not an extrapolation beyond the design, only beyond the rows on disk

method.bootstrap: paired run-block bootstrap: draw n turns per arm, drawing runs with replacement then turns within the pooled runs; two 200-resample percentile intervals per pair; disjoint when they do not overlap; 1000 outer pairs
method.diagnostic_ignoring_floor: n < 60 rows also report the fraction computed WITHOUT the frozen tail floor, only to make the old request-n card comparable; those are not admissible readings
method.estimator: analyze_stats.quantile_ci(values, q, resamples=10000, seed=20261026); refuses when n < 20 or n*(1-q) < 3
method.run_block_definition: a run = one (rows file, arm, rep) group. Every longrun file on disk carries rep=1, so each arm has exactly 1 block: a run bootstrap with 1 block is DEGENERATE and collapses to a turn bootstrap. The launch grid (3 runs/arm) has 3 blocks; the design reading uses n_eff = runs x n_eff_within_run.
method.selector: analyze_stats.turn_latency_rows(rows) -> (selected, meta); one row per (arm, rep, turn_index); kind="tool-followup" is never a turn
method.stop_rule: stop_reason in {length, runaway_turn} or truncated=true dropped from the latency population, counted

question: re-derive the power verdict with the turn denominator the analyser uses; can the 1,016-request grid adjudicate H1?

verdict_forcing_numbers.statement: the 1,016-request grid gives the H1 pair 144 raw turns/arm = 3 runs x 48. That clears the raw floor (144 >= 60) but is worth only 31.36 effective timings on pointer-stable (lag-1 0.6423), 52% of the 60 floor, and no single cell in it can publish a p95 at all. It clears the floor only under the pooled r=0.3921 reading (62.89). To clear it on the binding arm it needs 276 -> 288 raw turns/arm: 1056 requests for a conformant four-arm grid (768 turns at 1.374532), which the remaining 3,192 afford.
